[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is nuclear RNA production and maturation: an RNA polymerase I subunit supports ribosomal RNA transcription, a small-subunit processome component participates in pre-rRNA processing toward ribosome assembly, a general transcription factor subunit assists RNA polymerase II promoter opening, a spliceosome-associated crooked-neck-like factor acts in pre-mRNA splicing, and a core exosome subunit provides 3' to 5' exoribonuclease-mediated RNA trimming and surveillance; loss of that exosome subunit causes cerebellar hypoplasia with spinal motor neuron degeneration. Together these activities set the cell's capacity for ribosome biogenesis and accurate mRNA output, and hence growth and protein synthesis.

[untitled BTM module] These genes sketch a morphogen-driven programme that patterns mesenchymal tissue and steers progenitors toward bone, cartilage, skin and blood-supporting fates. BMP signalling sits at its centre: SMAD1 carries the receptor signal to the nucleus, ZNF521 acts as a nuclear cofactor tuning that output in skeletal and haematopoietic progenitors, while secreted GREM1 antagonises BMP ligands to keep niches permissive, and INHBA contributes an activin/TGF-beta arm through its own receptor-SMAD route.

[untitled BTM module] These genes converge on cyclic AMP as an intracellular messenger and on the cells that depend on it. Two calcium/calmodulin-stimulated adenylate cyclases, ADCY1 and ADCY8, generate cAMP in neurons in response to calcium entry, coupling synaptic activity to kinase signalling and long-term potentiation; the serotonin receptor HTR6 and a G protein gamma subunit sit upstream of the same second-messenger route, while CAMK2N1 restrains calcium/calmodulin-dependent kinase II and so tunes the calcium arm of the response.

[untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is transmembrane solute handling in polarized epithelia of liver and kidney, coupled to regulated vesicular secretion. Several members are plasma-membrane carriers that set how nutrients and ions cross epithelial barriers: GLUT2 moves glucose across hepatocyte and beta-cell membranes and underlies glucose sensing, the organic cation transporter SLC22A2 clears cationic drugs and metabolites in the proximal tubule, SLC6A13 imports betaine and GABA, and the copper-transporting ATPase ATP7B loads copper onto ceruloplasmin and excretes excess into bile, its loss causing Wnson disease.
